Peremyshlyany Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the older of Peremyshlyany's Jewish cemeteries, its oldest found gravestones dating to the 1720s, presumably indicating establishment in the early 18th century. Jews are first documented in Peremyshlyany in 1581, and a Hasidic dynasty was founded there in the 18th century; in 1875, the town hosted the first colonization society in Galicia dedicated to assisting Jewish resettlement to Eretz Israel. The Jewish population reached 2,934 (62 percent) by the beginning of the 20th century. Following the German occupation of 1939, around 600 Jews were executed on the banks of the San River; after the Nazis returned on July 1, 1941, nearly 400 more were executed that November, and about 2,500 were deported to Bełżec in November 1942. A ghetto liquidated on May 22, 1943 saw more than 2,000 Jews executed.
